newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee steadies vs forward dlr, RBI buys spot.
newsitem.headline: India rupee steadies vs forward dlr, RBI buys spot.

text.p: The Indian rupee steadied against the forward dollar on Tuesday afternoon after slipping mildly early in the day, dealers said.

Dealers at two leading banks said the initial spurt in forward premiums reflected either short-covering or profit- taking. There was no sign of firms beginning to cover to take advantage of the low premiums, they said.
"There is no import demand," said a dealer.
Six month annualised forward dollar premiums touched a 32-month low of 3.25 percent on Monday.

In the spot market, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Tuesday bought dollars below the 35.82 mark, scotching early morning speculation the RBI may not intervene as latest money supply figures showed M3 growth exceeding RBI targets.
RBI's latest data showed M3 money supply growth at 16.6 percent against its target of 15.0-15.5 percent for the year.

RBI closed its annual accounts on June 30 and many dealers were eagerly looking for any sign of a change in stance. But RBI's resumption of dollar purchases showed there was no change in its policy of halting the rupee's rise by buying dollars.
Commerce minister Bola Bulli Ramaiah's statement earlier on Tuesday he was not happy with the rupee's exchange rate did not impact the market, dealers said.
"Maybe exporters may go slow on their forward sales for the next few days," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
Exporters have been selling far forward, including June 1998 delivery, on Tuesday, dealers said.
Asked when India would make the rupee fully convertible, Ramaiah said: "Full convertibility only when there is a surplus on the trade account."
India reported a merchandise trade deficit of $5.44 billion in 1996/97 (April-March), up from $4.54 billion a year ago.
